subject: Learning Methods
title: Building a Learning Identity
description: A quick win: understand Building a Learning Identity.

hook.text: People who say 'I don't' instead of 'I can't' when refusing temptation are 8 times more likely to follow through.

buildup.text: Language shapes identity. 'I don't skip study sessions' is an identity claim.

discovery.text: A learning identity makes studying the default, not the exception. You don't negotiate each session. Learners learn.

twist.text: Identity shifts slowly. You become a learner one study session at a time.

climax.text: Declare yourself a lifelong learner. Back it with one small action daily. Identity is the ultimate habit anchor.

punchline.text: Don't versus can't. Identity is the strongest anchor.

quiz.question: Why is 'I don't' more effective than 'I can't' for behavior change?
options: It sounds more polite to others
'I don't' is an identity claim; 'I can't' implies an external restriction you want to break
Negative self-talk is always more effective than positive
